original_answer: Yes, the query-bag matching model uses neural networks. The paper's model (QBM) includes a mutual coverage component based on the cross-attention matrix of the query-bag pair [8], and it employs an hCNN component, a CNN-based matching model in which the query and a question in the bag are fed into a CNN respectively, with the cross-attention matrix fed into another CNN to obtain the interaction representation [5]. The introduction also notes that researchers have adopted deep neural networks to model matching relationships in related text matching work [1].

cited_sources.text: To our knowl- edge, there is no query-bag matching study exists, and we focus on the new approach in this paper. Recalling the text matching task [7], recently, researchers have adopted the deep neural network to model the matching relation- ship. ESIM [2] judges the inference relationship between two sen- tences by enhanced LSTM and interaction space. SMN [6] performs the context-response matching for the open-domain dialog system.

hCNN is a CNN based matching model which is fast enough to work on the industry application. The input of hCNN is a query q and the i-th question bi in the bag. q and bi are fed into a CNN respectively. A cross-attention matrix Mi is fed into another CNN to get the interaction representation between them. Each element of Mi is defined as Mi a,b = q⊤a · bi,b where qa is the word embedding of the a-th word in query q and bi,b is the embedding of the b-th word in bi.

In this paper, we propose a simple but effective mutual coverage component to model the above-mentioned problem. The coverage is based on the cross-attention matrix of the query-bag pair which in- dicates the matching degree of elements between the query and bag. The mutual coverage is performed by stacking the cross-attention matrix along two directions, i.e., query and bag, in the word level respectively.
